AL1_dueDiligence.subject: Aligrithm — aligrithm.com (Ali H. Askar, CQF)
AL1_dueDiligence.whatItIs: a solo-authored quantitative-trading research publication with real methodological depth (CSCV/PBO, backtest-overfitting discipline, research hygiene)
AL1_dueDiligence.scope: ZERO DeFi / on-chain scope — no protocol, no data feed, no contract tooling
AL1_dueDiligence.why: NOT a competitor (different domain — systematic trading research, not a DeFi trust screen), NOT a data source (nothing on-chain), NOT a technology source (nothing to import). The value is a reading reference on multiple-testing discipline — a map, not the territory. Nothing integrates on any path.
AL1_dueDiligence.consequence: the classification is durable — it prevents wasted future diligence cycles; a future 'should we look at Aligrithm again?' is answered here
AL1_dueDiligence.integrationForbidden: a repo imported from Aligrithm, or the blog cited as authority for a load-bearing method, is a drift the wall catches (findings_closed_groundtruth); load-bearing claims cite the PRIMARY papers below

AL3_AL5_primaryCitations.rule: the Stamp's load-bearing statistical methods cite their PRIMARY sources — the peer-reviewed / SSRN paper, NEVER a blog; Aligrithm is a reading reference only

methods.method: the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (the Stamp's significance; src/backtest/py/rigor.py::psr/dsr)
methods.primary: Bailey, D. H. & López de Prado, M. (2014). The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality. The Journal of Portfolio Management, 40(5), 94-107.

methods.method: the Probability of Backtest Overfitting / CSCV (the multiple-testing deflation companion; parked behind the trigger)
methods.primary: Bailey, D. H., Borwein, J. M., López de Prado, M. & Zhu, Q. J. (2016). The Probability of Backtest Overfitting. Journal of Computational Finance, 20(4), 39-69.

methods.method: Optimal Number of Clusters (ONC — deterministic strategy-family clustering; parked)
methods.primary: López de Prado, M. & Lewis, M. J. (2019). Detection of False Investment Strategies Using Unsupervised Learning Methods. Quantitative Finance, 19(9), 1555-1565.

AL4_AL6_pboTrigger.what: a deterministic CSCV/PBO companion metric becomes buildable in the opt-in Stamp WHEN AND ONLY WHEN the future proposer emits ≥ 20-50 trials per strategy family (the SAME trigger that makes the familyN deflation live)
AL4_AL6_pboTrigger.pinnedTrigger: ≥ 20-50 trials/family — PINNED so it cannot drift; below the trigger the PBO/CSCV companion stays PARKED
AL4_AL6_pboTrigger.implementationAbsent: the frozen rigor.py contains the anti-PBO adjudicator math (CSCV/PBO/CPCV per Lopez de Prado Appendix B, byte-frozen, carried from the monorepo) but it is INERT on the single-trial Stamp path (familyN=1 -> no multiple-testing charge; RE3 renders 'the deflation is currently inert'). What is ASSERTED ABSENT is a NEW CSCV/PBO COMPANION -- a module OUTSIDE the frozen core that assembles >= 20-50 trials/family and surfaces a live overfitting metric below the trigger; a grep wall asserts no such companion exists (a seeded pbo.ts/cscv.ts companion on the path fails the wall)
AL4_AL6_pboTrigger.extendsRE5: extends Moat's RE5 trials-ledger schema convention (the trials-ledger is this companion's future input)
AL4_AL6_pboTrigger.renderStatesInert: the Stamp render already states the deflation is currently inert (RE3: '1 attempt counted, no multiple-testing penalty was paid') — the PBO companion is the future deepening of that same charge, not a hidden live metric
